data.content_ref: inline:The target's claim that the preference is defensible 'only by accepting a non-probabilistic metaphysical commitment to verisimilitude' is factually incomplete and misleading regarding Popper's own terms. It ignores Popper's explicit pragmatic solution: the methodological rule to prefer the better-corroborated theory as the one that has withstood the severest tests so far, without asserting it is closer to the truth. By framing the defense as requiring a metaphysical leap to 'truth-likeness,' the target constructs a false dilemma that omits the actual pragmatic decision rule Popper advocated to avoid induction.
